title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
task: Mapping 3D spatial organization of desmin intermediate filaments in muscle sarcomeres
key_results: dSTORM and SIM microscopy revealed desmin extends from Z-lines into sarcomere interior aligned with actin filaments; dominant-negative desmin inhibition selectively reduced active tension at longer sarcomere lengths
comments: The finding that desmin extends along actin rather than remaining confined to Z-discs substantially revises the structural model of sarcomeric organization and mechanical function.

outputs: active tension vs. sarcomere length measurements

hypotheses.hypothesis: Desmin filaments are confined to Z-lines
hypotheses.result: Refuted; desmin extends into sarcomere interior aligned with actin

hypotheses.hypothesis: Desmin contributes to force production, particularly at longer sarcomere lengths
hypotheses.result: Supported; disrupted desmin selectively reduced tension at longer lengths

title: Common misconceptions in life sciences about the concentrations and toxicity of perchlorates on Mars
task: Clarifying perchlorate toxicity misconceptions for Mars habitability research
key_results: Identified systematic misconceptions in perchlorate concentration estimates and toxicity mechanisms relevant to Martian environments and bioprocessing systems
comments: This is primarily a critical review article addressing conceptual errors rather than presenting new experimental data, limiting quantitative validation.

title: Spatial reprogramming of AP-1 complexes by mutant p53 flips the transcriptional output of the FOSL1 enhancer-promoter axis to drive migration
task: Elucidate how mutant p53 reprograms AP-1 complexes to drive EMT and migration
key_results: Wild-type p53 silences FOSL1 via c-JUN/ATF2 repression at CREs in intron 1; mutant p53 redirects c-JUN/FRA1 complexes to TREs in promoter, establishing self-reinforcing activation loop driving migration
comments: The spatial rewiring of AP-1 binding sites represents an elegant GOF mechanism, though the therapeutic window for disrupting these complexes without affecting normal p53 function requires careful evaluation.

model_io.model: FOSL1 enhancer-promoter axis in cancer cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mutant p53 flips transcriptional output at FOSL1 locus by redirecting AP-1 complexes from intronic CREs to promoter TREs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: mutp53 drives c-JUN/FRA1 activation at promoter TREs while wtp53 maintains repression via c-JUN/ATF2 at intronic CREs

title: Heparan sulfate sulfatases are essential for the patterning of human stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons
task: Identify extracellular regulators controlling midbrain dopaminergic neuron patterning from human iPSCs
key_results: SULF1/2 loss increases 6-O-sulfated heparan sulfate and disrupts anteroposterior and dorsoventral patterning; knockout cells adopt hindbrain/spinal cord identity instead of ventral midbrain; FGF inhibition partially rescues midbrain fate but not ventral specification
comments: This work reveals an underappreciated layer of extracellular control via heparan sulfate sulfatases, though complete restoration of ventral identity requires additional mechanisms beyond FGF pathway modulation.

model_io.model: Human iPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neuron differentiation

hypotheses.hypothesis: SULF1/2 are essential for mDA neuron patterning via heparan sulfate remodeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SULF1/2 knockout disrupts anteroposterior and dorsoventral patterning, redirecting cells to alternative fates

hypotheses.hypothesis: Altered FGF signaling mediates patterning defects in SULF1/2 knockout
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed: FGF inhibition redirects cells toward midbrain identity but fails to restore ventral specification

title: A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors
task: Quantify chromatin sensitivity dependence across transcription factors
key_results: Chromatin sensitivity forms a continuum across TFs, correlating with motif strength; regulation occurs via mixed hierarchical and cooperative mechanisms in locus-specific manner
comments: Deep learning framework resolves a longstanding debate but lacks explicit quantitative benchmarks for model accuracy or sensitivity estimates.

model_io.model: Deep learning framework for chromatin sensitivity assessment

hypotheses.result: Rejected; sensitivity is a continuum, not hierarchical

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multiple TFs bind cooperatively to overcome chromatin barriers
hypotheses.result: Partially supported; mixed hierarchical and cooperative mechanisms operate locus-specifically

title: Late-stage clinical development pathways for Lassa fever vaccines: scientific, operational, and regulatory considerations
task: Identify feasible clinical development pathways for Lassa fever vaccine licensure
key_results: No quantitative results reported; focus on regulatory and operational pathways given absence of protective biomarker and low seasonal incidence
comments: Strategic review document addressing trial design constraints rather than presenting novel experimental data or validation results.

title: Stromal enriched metastatic decider drives lymph node metastasis in lung adenocarcinoma
task: Identify metastasis-associated spatial niches and biomarkers in lung adenocarcinoma lymph node dissemination
key_results: CYP24A1 enrichment in stromal-enriched metastatic decider (SEED) spots associated with poorer prognosis; CYP24A1+ malignant subpopulation exhibits IFNγ-associated transcriptional features
comments: Spatial transcriptomics approach provides mechanistic insight, but prognostic association relies on retrospective cohort (n=8) and requires prospective validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: SEED regions represent metastasis-permissive ecosystems at tumor-stroma interfaces
hypotheses.result: Supported; SEED domains enriched at tumor-stroma interfaces with associated transcriptional signatures

hypotheses.hypothesis: CYP24A1 marks a pro-metastatic malignant subpopulation
hypotheses.result: Supported; CYP24A1+ cells show IFNγ-associated features and correlate with worse prognosis

title: Multimodal digital biomarker for asthma: complementary roles of vocal, clinical and demographic factors
task: Asthma identification via multimodal voice and clinical data integration
key_results: AUROC 0.83 and Brier score 0.18; reading-passage modality weighted higher in cases with greater respiratory symptom burden
comments: Promising proof-of-concept but relies on self-reported asthma status without spirometric confirmation, limiting clinical validity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multimodal integration outperforms unimodal acoustic approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; multimodal AUROC 0.83 exceeded unimodal performance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Respiratory symptom burden alters which voice modality is predictive
hypotheses.result: Supported; reading-passage weighting increased with symptom burden

title: Strain-driven and electric-field-tunable self-morphotropic phase boundary in nitride perovskite
task: Design high-piezoelectricity nitride perovskite via strain-tunable morphotropic phase boundary
key_results: Piezoelectric coefficients exceed AlN/AlScN/GaScN by orders of magnitude; electric-field-tunable self-morphotropic phase boundary demonstrated in LaWN3
comments: First-principles prediction of ultrahigh piezoelectricity in nitride perovskites is promising but requires experimental validation of the predicted phase transitions and piezoelectric response.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Biaxial strain induces sequential symmetry progression enabling polarization rotation
hypotheses.result: Self-morphotropic phase boundary identified with ultrahigh piezoelectric response

hypotheses.hypothesis: Electric field can dynamically tune the morphotropic phase boundary

title: Microstructural changes in radiochromic film and dosimetry in magnetic field
task: Validate radiochromic film dosimetry accuracy in magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy
key_results: Optical density measurements show negligible dosimetric differences (within experimental uncertainty) between magnetic field (0.35 T) and no-field conditions across 2–16 Gy; crystal structures align to ±80–100° with field but total polymerized material quantity unchanged
comments: The key insight that magnetic fields affect polymerization directionality without changing total polymer quantity elegantly resolves conflicting literature and validates EBT-3 for MR-linac dosimetry.

model_io.model: Scanning electron microscopy and image analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnetic field presence affects dosimetric accuracy of EBT-3 films
hypotheses.result: Refuted: negligible dosimetric differences observed; optical density unaffected

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnetic field influences polymerization process directionality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: crystal angular alignment shows pronounced clustering at ±80–100° versus random 360° distribution

title: Quantitative evaluation of single-grating phase-contrast imaging with a femtosecond laser–plasma K $$\alpha$$ X-ray source
task: Quantitatively evaluate single-grating phase-contrast X-ray imaging with femtosecond laser-plasma source
key_results: Phase image correlation score of 0.922 ± 0.008 between theory and experiment; Confidence Map metric validates self-consistency of phase retrieval across varying source coherence and photon flux conditions
comments: The parametric study effectively disentangles source coherence and flux effects on phase retrieval fidelity, providing a systematic framework for optimizing exposure-resolution trade-offs in time-resolved imaging.

model_io.model: Single 2D-grating phase-contrast imaging system with femtosecond laser-plasma Kα X-ray source

hypotheses.hypothesis: Single-grating phase retrieval with laser-plasma Kα source achieves high-fidelity quantitative phase measurement
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: correlation score 0.922 ± 0.008 for known test object

hypotheses.hypothesis: X-ray source characteristics (coherence and flux) can be optimized to minimize exposure while preserving phase retrieval accuracy
hypotheses.result: Supported: parametric study identifies trade-off regimes between fixed photon-count and fixed acquisition-time conditions
